title: The 28 listed HD 139139 dips do not reject independent arrivals in a spacing test
abstract: We test even spacing in the 28 known HD 139139 dip times. A live-time spacing test gives a lower-tail fraction of 0.06166 under independent constant-rate detections with the total count fixed. A four-hour minimum separation between detections raises the fraction to 0.11747. Removal of the suspect dip gives 0.04243 without a separation rule, but 0.08093 with the four-hour rule. Thus the weak evidence for even spacing does not survive these simple selection controls. Moderate regularity has low detection power in synthetic tests. The test is exploratory and uses the same K2 events as earlier work. It does not confirm a planet, a physical recovery time, or an independent detection. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact source hashes and retrieval steps are included. External source records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Spacing dispersion under independent detections and lower-tail fractions under minimum-separation controls.
